sentences.text: That flash overhead? The air inside it can get as hot as fifty thousand degrees Fahrenheit. That's five times hotter than the surface of the sun.
But thunder isn't the lightning itself. It's the air.
The flash heats nearby air in a split second. It expands so fast it compresses the air ahead of it, a shock wave, a bit like a sonic boom.
Right after, the air cools and snaps back. That fast expansion and contraction is the sound wave we hear as thunder.
A sharp crack means the bolt was close. A low rumble means it was several miles away or more. You hear the nearest part first, then the farther parts.
And you can usually hear thunder only about ten miles out.
So, if the sky can flash-heat air hotter than the sun, is thunder the sky showing off... or just yelling at us to go inside?
